wv_upper_rock_city.blurb: Upper Rock City is one of the main bouldering zones in Coopers Rock State Forest, above the Cheat River canyon east of Morgantown. Big blocks of the forest’s sandstone sit scattered through the woods in a fairly compact area, so you can move from problem to problem on foot. It is nearly all bouldering, with a handful of top-rope and trad lines, and the grades spread widely: lots of V0 to V5, a good number of V6 and V7, and a few problems up to V10. Tomb Raider Area, Entrance Boulders and The Sea hold the most problems. Across the forest, spring and fall are generally the best seasons, and the canopy shades the summer, though humidity and wet rock can interfere. It is one of the busier zones.

az_east_stronghold_bouldering.blurb: East Stronghold Bouldering is the bouldering side of Cochise Stronghold, in the Dragoon Mountains of southeastern Arizona. The rock is granite with weathered, patinated surfaces, in a remote and rugged setting of tall granite domes. It is almost all bouldering, with an even spread of difficulty from V0 up to V10 and beyond, and many unclimbed lines remain. The main concentration of problems is around the central boulder fields, with Klettergarten and Roke Knoll further out. The stronghold gets plenty of sun, making it a popular winter destination; fall through spring is the best window, and summer heat is severe.

mi_550_roped.blurb: 550 Roped is the climbing along County Road 550 north of Marquette in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. It is a varied cluster: Sugarloaf Mountain, a popular hiking summit with moderate sport and top-rope routes and some bouldering; Wetmore Pond, with boulder problems on gneiss outcrops in a boggy wetland; and Hogback Mountain, with a mix of trad, sport and top-rope lines. Bouldering, sport and trad are all present, with a few winter ice routes. Roped climbs run from 5.4 up to the low 5.12s, mostly in the 5.6 to 5.11 range, and the boulder problems are mostly V0 to V3 with some harder ones.

ny_poke_o_moonshine.blurb: Poke-O-Moonshine is a peak at the eastern end of the northeastern Adirondacks, overlooking Interstate 87 on the Lake Champlain side. Steep cliffs of granite, about 600 feet high, ring its east and south sides, and the Main Face is the heart of the climbing. This is mostly a trad crag, with a smaller number of sport routes, a few boulders and some waterfall ice. Rock climbs run from the 5.6 range to 5.12, with the bulk at 5.9 to 5.12. The best-known pitches are long and exposed, and the climbing is serious rather than plentiful at easy grades. Headwall, the Second Tier and the Waterfall Area add variety.

or_broughton_bluff.blurb: Broughton Bluff is an easy-to-reach crag at the western mouth of the Columbia River Gorge, near Troutdale and Portland. Its roughly dozen cliffs are made of jumbled basalt and sit largely under tree canopy, which keeps them cool on hot days. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with trad concentrated at places like the North Face and Hanging Gardens. Grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.12, with plenty of 5.13 too and a few easier lines. Bat Wall and Jungle Cliff are the biggest sport walls, and Red Wall is also popular. Late spring, summer and fall are best; winter tends to be damp unless you climb 5.12 or harder.

sd_outlets.blurb: The Outlets are a cluster of granite spires and formations behind Sylvan Lake in Custer State Park, in the Black Hills at about 6,000 feet. The rock is sharp, strong granite, and most of the climbing is face climbing that can be bold, with bolts spaced far apart and gear often placeable between them. Trad dominates, with a good number of sport routes. Grades run from 5.5 to 5.13, with most between 5.8 and 5.12, so confidence at the grade matters. Inner Outlet and Outer Outlet hold the most routes, and the back side of the dam, Vertigo and Sunday Gulch add more. The sun can be strong, so early or late in the day is more comfortable. Rappels are usually needed to get down from summits.
